# Automatic differentiation as a first class citizen

## What does it mean to say a package supports AD?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
- A real model needs a PPL, and a PPL needs gradients through every
  component. AD is a requirement, not a feature
- Nobody has written down what supporting AD means, so we picked a
  definition and made CI defend it
- `DifferentiationInterfaceTest` does the correctness testing. On top,
  a package declares which scenarios are broken on which backend, and
  CI re-runs them

::: {.callout-note}
Is there a guide for any of this anywhere in the Julia ecosystem? I
went looking and did not find one.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
```julia
const _AD_BACKENDS = [
  (header = "ForwardDiff", ...),
  (header = "ReverseDiff (tape)", ...),
  (header = "Enzyme forward", ...),
  (header = "Enzyme reverse", ...),
  (header = "Mooncake reverse", ...),
  (header = "Mooncake forward", ...),
]
```

::: {.attribution}
Abridged from `_AD_BACKENDS`, `src/scaffold.jl:1464` in
`EpiAwarePackageTools.jl`, read 2026-08-11. Each entry also carries a
Codecov flag, a test item tag and the package it loads, and the list
generates the CI matrix, the flags, the README badges and the support
table in the docs · `check_broken` and the registry contract are in
`src/ad_harness.jl` ·
[DifferentiationInterfaceTest.jl](https://github.com/JuliaDiff/DifferentiationInterface.jl).
:::
:::
::::

## A wrong number, not an error

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
```julia
f(x) = xlogy(x[1], 0.8)   # d/dx = log(0.8)

DI.gradient(f, DI.AutoForwardDiff(), [0.0])
DI.gradient(f, DI.AutoMooncake(), [0.0])
```

| Backend | Gradient at `x = 0` |
|---|---|
| Finite differences | -0.22314 |
| ForwardDiff | -0.22314 |
| ReverseDiff | -0.22314 |
| Enzyme | -0.22314 |
| Mooncake | **0.0** |
:::
::: {.column width="52%"}
- `logpdf(Gamma(k, θ), x)` computes `xlogy(k - 1, x / θ)`. Mooncake has
  no rule for `xlogy`, so it differentiates the implementation. At shape
  1.0 the first argument is zero, the `iszero` branch returns a
  constant, and the gradient comes back as zero
- Nothing throws. The sampler runs. The number is wrong
- `EpiAwareADTools.jl` carries the rule, and deletes it the day
  Mooncake ships one

::: {.attribution}
The three lines and the backend comparison are from
[ComposedDistributions.jl#99][cd99], 2026-07-07. `xlogy` comes from
`LogExpFunctions`, `DI` is `DifferentiationInterface`. Mooncake 0.5.37,
Julia 1.12 · the withdrawn upstream report is
[chalk-lab/Mooncake.jl#1241][mc1241], closed the day it was opened, and
nothing has replaced it as of 2026-08-11 · the local rule is
`ext/EpiAwareADToolsLogExpFunctionsMooncakeExt.jl`.
:::
:::
::::

## Nobody can tell you which backend a model needs

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
| Backend | `Censored` | `Composed` |
|---|---|---|
| ForwardDiff | green | red |
| ReverseDiff, tape | green | red |
| Mooncake forward | green | red |
| Mooncake reverse | green | red |
| Enzyme forward | green, 1 broken | red |
| Enzyme reverse | green, 1 broken | red |

::: {.attribution}
`Censored` is `CensoredDistributions.jl`, `Composed` is
`ComposedDistributions.jl` · declared broken scenarios in
[CensoredDistributions.jl#889][cd889], read from `test/ADFixtures` on
`main` · last `AD` run on `main` green 2026-06-21 there and red on all
six 2026-08-07 in `ComposedDistributions.jl` ·
[TuringLang/ADTests][adtests], archived 2026-06-15.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
- DifferentiationInterface tells you about a function. Turing tells you
  what Turing tests. Nothing tells you about a model assembled from
  five packages that each tested on their own
- The one public per-backend table for a probabilistic programming
  stack, `TuringLang/ADTests`, was archived in June
- In my view none of the six is reliably best, and each is kept going
  by a small team
:::
::::
